title: AI Safety Is Mostly A Sex Cult In Berkeley, California
author: SE Gyges
html:
These people shouldn’t make policy.

There has been a great effort over many years to distance AI Safety discussion from its origin and intellectual center, because its center is a predatory sex cult started by a fan fiction author. Since those involved want to be taken seriously, they have to hide that. Everyone else working in AI Safety is, effectively, a smokescreen for this core group and their ideas.

We might some day have “AI Safety”, as a science or policy area, that is not primarily a sex cult in Berkeley, California, but it does not currently exist.

Who Is Eliezer Yudkowsky?

This is Eliezer Yudkowsky. He is seen here in a meeting with Bernie Sanders, who he is advising on AI policy, and in The AI Doc, now on Netflix.

This is Yudkowsky in Time Magazine in 2023, advocating in favor of risking nuclear war to prevent AI research from happening anywhere on Earth.

This is very senior OpenAI employee and unofficial OpenAI spokesman Roon. Roon’s opinion of Yudkowsky is that:

  1. Yudkowsky is in and/or running a sex cult.

  2. Yudkowsky’s opinions about AI are important, and should be taken seriously.

This seems to be an extremely common pair of opinions concerning Yudkowsky.

Yudkowsky is sufficiently controversial that people motivated by his ideas often downplay or deny his influence. Sometimes this spans multiple layers: People who received money from Sam Bankman-Fried denying they’re Effective Altruists, Sam Bankman-Fried denying he’s an Effective Altruist when caught, Effective Altruists denying their version of AI Safety is heavily influenced by Yudkowsky’s, people literally attending the same orgies as Yudkowsky passing themselves off as merely “rationalist adjacent”, and so on. But Yudkowsky is provably, publicly influential on essentially all major public figures in AI. It is easy to deny not because it is hidden but because it seems so insane.

Yudkowsky is the person who connected Shane Legg and Demis Hassabis to Peter Thiel so that they could secure funding to start DeepMind1, which is now Google's AI research division. Here's Sam Altman's opinion of Yudkowsky.

This is the schedule for the Future of Life Institute's conference on AI in Puerto Rico in January, 2015. Elon Musk would found OpenAI that December. So it seems plausible that his attendance did influence the founding of OpenAI.

Dario Amodei, current CEO of Anthropic, is here in 2013 identified as a "member of the Effective Altruism community" on the blog of Yudkowsky's non-profit.

And here he is arguing about the paperclip maximizer, a now-classic thought experiment, originally Yudkowsky’s, about an AI that might kill everyone.

“AI Alignment” and “AI Safety” were first popularized by Yudkowsky’s non-profit, MIRI, the Machine Intelligence Research Institute. OpenAI and Anthropic have cited Yudkowsky or his non-profit at least a dozen times, and the entire way we talk about AI uses terminology his non-profit popularized. It is effectively impossible to even discuss these areas without, implicitly or explicitly, performing commentary on Yudkowsky’s writing.

This is Jacob Coxon, the recent “whistleblower” who quit Anthropic, being asked his opinions on rationalists and effective altruists.

This is Nate Silver citing LessWrong as a source of major information about AI risk. LessWrong is a website started by Yudkowsky in 2009, and originally filled only with his writing.

This is Oliver Habryka, who runs the nonprofit controlling LessWrong and the rationalist’s compound, known as Lighthaven, explaining how large he thinks the influence of rationalism is on AI Safety and AI existential risk discourse. He is engaged in some kind of internal territorial dispute here. It is possibly the only time I have ever agreed with him.

This is a podcast interview with Daniel Alejandro Moreno-Gama, who attempted to firebomb Sam Altman’s house, in which he names Yudkowsky as his primary influence.

Who Are The Rationalists?

Yudkowsky’s more dedicated followers seem to prefer to call themselves “the rationality community” these days, everyone else calls them “rationalists”, the entire following “rationalism”. I generally prefer “rats”.

This is a long denial that they are a religion. I alternate between finding it funny and finding it insulting.

The fan fiction that launched a thousand cults is Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality, or HPMOR. It is possibly the highest-impact single modern religious text, rivalled only by the Book of Mormon. Its influence may not yet have peaked. It is the holy book of the first great internet cult.

How Are Rationalists Connected To The Bay Area Effective Altruists?

Allegedly, Effective Altruism and its AI safety efforts are a separate thing and not directly beholden to Yudkowsky. This is fundamentally not true. Effective Altruism in the Bay Area has almost perfect overlap with rationalism, and the Effective Altruist AI Safety people in the Bay set the agenda for the rest of Effective Altruism’s safety efforts.

In the Bay Area, Rationalism and Effective Altruism are the same people, at the same events, in the same places, who believe the things said by the same authors and leaders, with only very slight differences between spheres of influence. Yudkowsky called himself an effective altruist and a rationalist until a peculiar internal schism. Scott Alexander, the second-most influential writer in the space, has usually called himself both. They generally work for the same companies and non-profits.

Frequently, Effective Altruists bring up all of Effective Altruism’s other charitable activities and its charming, benevolent members who don’t live in the Bay Area to deflect true criticisms of the Bay Area Effective Altruist community. This effectively makes their other charitable operations and workers shields and fronts for the priorities and behavior of the Effective Altruists in the Bay Area, who are interested almost exclusively in AI.

Where there is any separation between the two things in the Bay, “rationalism” is people and things more closely tied to Yudkowsky, and “effective altruism” has had a few institutional centers but is currently focused around Anthropic and its CEO, Dario Amodei. They compete for attention and funding in that space. Yudkowsky’s position is that AI will definitely kill us, and Dario’s position is that AI is ten to twenty-five percent likely to kill us.

Both are saying what justifies giving them and no one else money, labor and attention. Since Yudkowsky is a writer and not a scientist of any kind, he can only claim that he and his organization are important and deserve money and prestige if AI Safety is an unsolvable problem and only advocating against AI matters. Since Dario leads a company that actually makes AI, he must claim that AI doom is a very large problem that only his company can manage.

Yudkowsky also claimed that his (non-profit) company was probably the only one that could make AI safely, back when AI companies seldom made anything and he could claim to be doing research by simply writing. This belief system has been strenuously improved for, among other things, being a pitch to investors, donors, volunteers and employees. It is also a pitch for people to give you total control over them, because if they do not, the world might end. After Yudkowsky refined this pitch and mostly used it to form a sex cult, modifications of it became the pitch for organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic, and this is integral to employee morale and recruiting because so many research staff are believers to one degree or another.

Yudkowsky is not going to stop preaching the gospel of doom, among other reasons because he is effectively paid for it and it is the only job he has ever had. He would stand to lose his social position and the roughly 600k in income he is paid out of his non-profit if he changed his tune. In general, if doom prophecies are worth money, people will produce more. This system’s purpose is to attract funding and young idealists and to find ways to spend the funding and make use of the young idealists. One of the ways that young idealists are made use of is by using them for sex, or introducing them to sex work.

People tend to follow their incentives.

EA impact on Anthropic, on policy

People sometimes deny that Anthropic is an Effective Altruist organization. This is a complete lie. Dario cheerfully identified as an Effective Altruist and debated about AI with Yudkowsky. Holden Karnofsky, Ben Mann, Daniela Amodei, Amanda Askell, and Jack Clark and Tom Brown are all Effective Altruists and have affiliated themselves with Effective Altruist pledges and causes.

Dario in particular is almost perfectly on-type for a Bay Area Effective Altruist in what he says and how he says it. Dario’s often bizarre, vague, and meandering writing style alone has no real precedent besides LessWrong and its AI-focused spinoff, Alignment Forum. Their company’s strategy is very close to the playbook Yudkowsky laid out, back before companies which were actually capable of doing science removed any credibility Yudkowsky’s organization had when it claimed to do AI research.

This same thing happens when it comes to the incestuous relationships between all of the other non-profits in the Bay that are meant to be focused on AI risk. They all have one of a few sources of funding and they recruit from the movement. Holden Karnofsky, currently Anthropic, formerly head of Coefficient Giving, was an original board member of Redwood Research and one of the initial champions for METR. Both are held up as independent organizations and are not. Redwood mostly seems to be trying to catch the same lightning in a bottle that Yudkowsky had with MIRI in inspiring devotion, to avoid behaving in any of the obviously disgraceful ways Yudkowsky is prone, and to launder essentially the same world view into policy papers that can be cited and pointed to as having come from a serious organization.

In the video with Bernie Sanders, the present people are:

  • Eliezer Yudkowsky, MIRI

  • Nate Soares, MIRI

  • Jeffrey Ladish (funded by Coefficient Giving, an EA charity)

  • Daniel Kokotajlo (funded by Survival and Flourishing Fund, an EA charity)

So when they go to get people to talk to a senator we have Yudkowsky, Yudkowsky’s top lieutenant, and two people whose paychecks are from Effective Altruist charities. We will be seeing three of these four again later.

Former Biden White House officials Bruce Reed and Ben Buchanan recently wrote an op-ed in which they deny having said that they wanted to ban open-source AI. They claim the first thing they were told in that meeting was to watch out for “the sex cult that wants to run America’s AI policy.”

They then deny being Effective Altruists.

Ben Buchanan worked for two years as Director of the CyberAI Project at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), which appears to have received roughly 90% of its funding from Coefficient Giving (then OpenPhilanthropy). Since May 2025, four months after the end of the Biden administration he has been working as a consultant for Anthropic.

Buchanan has a book, published March 2022, in which he discusses the possibility of export controlling GPUs. In October 2022, the Biden administration put in place export restrictions for GPUs.

I read Buchanan’s book2, and I think he is probably not an Effective Altruist because his ideas are not weird enough; but since 2019, his salary has come either from Effective Altruism or from the White House. I am reasonably sure he comes by his opinions honestly, and believes in them for normal policy advisor reasons. If he changes his opinions his career is probably in trouble.

In spite of being often considered disgraceful and now being somewhat starved for cash, Yudkowsky and the organizations most closely tied to him are still, by far, the most influential sources of thinking about AI safety in the Bay and therefore on Earth. Because so many investors and key staff members hold him and his ideas in high regard, it is not clear that companies can directly disown him, although for example when Dario says to be less religious or less obsessed with “doom”, he appears to be positioning himself to try to carve influence away.

Paperclips, Doom

Yudkowsky’s most viral idea, the one that infects the most people and spreads the farthest, is that AI, if we continue to develop it, will

  1. certainly recursively self-improve, quickly achieving superintelligence (”RSI”),

  2. certainly escape human control,

  3. certainly kill everyone (”paperclip them”, “doom”).

All arguments about AI Safety and AI Alignment are primarily about mitigating this exact scenario under his exact terms. Significant modification is relatively rare. Where lower probabilities of doom than “certain” are given, people seem to still generally worry exclusively about Yudkowsky’s rough scenario: a sudden, unpredictable sequence of 1) superintelligence, 2) immediate escape from control, and 3) the death of all humans on Earth. This is always, implicitly, what "safety" and "alignment" are about.

These ideas occasionally veer into believing AI is magic. When presented as serious science and policy, this sort of thing is omitted.

Ordinarily, the play here would be to disown this and other concrete statements of his about AI doom as irrelevant. Of course we aren’t just repeating Yudkowsky! We are smart, normal people who believe normal things for normal reasons. Compare it, however, to AI 2027, allegedly a serious policy document, written by Daniel Kokotajlo and Scott Alexander, presenting its doom scenario.

This is a genre of science fiction that has a doomsday cult built around it. There are only slight modifications to the basic belief system. Somehow, maybe by just throwing money at it, taking these ideas seriously has been rendered prestigious or at least not too disgraceful, such that Kokotajlo, credited on the above, gets to advise Bernie Sanders. JD Vance was asked about this piece by Ross Douthat at the New York Times, and said he had read it. (In my opinion, on close reading AI 2027’s primary intended audience was clearly JD Vance.)

Essentially all of AI safety is rationalizations over Eliezer Yudkowsky’s ideas and there is no other substance to it. It is smokescreens, and Eliezer Yudkowsky.

This is his actual plan: to halt all AI research, all across the Earth, and instead do genetic engineering eugenics for a generation. Pause AI, stop AI, slowdown, pacing the frontier, they are all smokescreens, rationalizations, or ways of watering down this plan. This is why there is never any real “after we pause”, or “we will unpause when”; this is the only actual plan, and the public front for the plan cannot say this because it is too stupid and too offensive to be spoken in public, except by Yudkowsky, who never stops talking and who is too fucking ridiculous for anyone on the outside to believe everyone listens to him.

Anyone who thinks this is not the plan is not in on the plan, or is part of some faction that simply has no real plan. If this describes you and you didn’t know that, I am sorry that this is how you found out.

He has long since deleted this post demonstrating what his idea of an acceptable outcome is; this is ordinarily implied and not stated.

This industry approaches regulation in this way because it has, at its core, a millenarian death cult that worships and fears AI, believes AI will end the world, feels compelled to create AI, and at least somewhat wants to destroy AI as an entire field.

I will repeat: I do not think that these people should be making policy. I would vastly prefer if this were merely some insane Bay Area drama that I could ignore, but this has been made a very public national and international concern.

The paperclip maximizer is a thought experiment from 2003 and of very little relevance at all. People are perpetually striving to find evidence for this theory because they already believe it is true, and take pains to interpret any research or security development in AI as evidence for this exact doom coming to pass. As things come up which contradict this scenario, as often they do, they are often not understood because they do not match the prophecy. Alternative explanations are so unthinkable that many people cannot even be told.

Doom seems to be the most infectious idea here because it activates the same neurosis that every apocalyptic or millenarian cult does. The world is going to end, and only I and my special group of people in the know can maybe stop it. (Also, you should give me money and have sex with me.)

You can argue with them in any way you like but it barely matters. It's not, mostly, something people believe for good reasons, and they will simply go back to complaining about the apocalypse as soon as you stop paying attention. There are enough of them that the belief is self-reinforcing; they can arrange their lives such that they essentially never talk to anyone who is not a believer.

Harry Potter fan fiction, of course, is especially popular with children, and many people have made this their belief system since they were teenagers.

Since recruitment largely happens on the internet, people are widely dispersed. Where they are gathered in person, it is mostly in various communes in Berkeley, California. They call their communes "group houses", maybe to make it sound less cultish. Most of the details of this are what you expect from "a commune in Berkeley".

Everyone is polyamorous, everyone attends the same events, everyone lives in group homes together, everyone venerates the same few authors, everyone is very worried about AI doom, and a lot of people are on psychedelic drugs. They are all very contrarian together.

Lots and lots of them work at AI companies and non-profits. The safety, red team and alignment teams seem especially afflicted, because that's the area you go on to worry about and try to work against AI doom, which you are sure is at least medium likely. Other members will seek work in finance, because Effective Altruism, by creed, says you should seek more money so you can give more to charity. Those most concerned with AI risk will tend to almost exclusively give to AI charities and not any other Effective Altruist concern.

As a whole, this is a religious movement. Not everyone takes marching orders; they’re united by an idea, not any particular structure. The vast network of Effective Altruists around the world working on other charitable concerns are basically irrelevant to AI Safety. The core people who mostly live together and attend events and especially orgies in Berkeley are a sex cult, and the ones that aren't directly involved are part of the wider movement and are first and foremost its recruiting funnel, funding, and labor base.

Any time you get more than a few people who are deeply concerned with AI doom together, it seems like their natural form of organization looks like a cult; the movement as a whole, internationally, is less of a cult than it is a cult factory. Some of these cults have gone very badly. One of them is the Zizians.

That rationalists form cults constantly has been previously examined. There are many causative factors, but the core one is just that the entire thing is, in and of itself, a millenarian doomsday cult. If you believe you’re saving the world, it justifies anything; you cannot go against the cause for any reason. This gives leaders, whether official or unofficial, immense power over their members.

Forming a separate cult is also how you carve off influence and ultimately power for yourself, separate from the wider movement. This tends to mean that people try to do it more. All of these power struggles make the details of all of this extremely noisy, chaotic, and difficult to explain.

When you cut through all the distractions, chaos, and power struggles, San Francisco Rationalism is the inner circle of San Francisco Effective Altruism, which is the inner circle of Effective Altruism globally. Power and especially intellectual leadership flow almost entirely outwards from SF Rationalism to SF Effective Altruism to Effective Altruism’s global AI safety efforts. Everything else about Effective Altruism is effectively a front.

All of this has been an open secret for years. Everyone knows. Everyone knows if they say anything it will be ignored. I am shocked that I have gotten as much attention as I have to the problem; so let me try to get everything that seems to be very important into the record.

A Brief History of Rationalism

What I am hoping to convey is that this is not many small things, it’s one big thing. All of this is tied together through ideology, funding, and key people.

Bay Area rationalists and effective altruists do not document their own history because it is disgraceful. Only their enemies deliberately keep records of what they have done and are doing.

They do however write constantly, but they do this mostly as a social activity. They have been writing essays, chattering, bragging, or engaging in some kind of drama constantly for the last fifteen years.

So you really just have to read a lot to put this together.3 Everything I am saying, as far as I am capable, is true, and I believe the vast majority is public record. I am just connecting the dots by putting one straight line through them.

90s-00s: Usenet, Transhumanism, Extropianism

In 1996, a 17-year-old Eliezer Yudkowsky joins Usenet and the Extropians mailing list. His more notable influences are Drexler’s book on nanotechnology, Kurzweil’s book on AI, and Nick Bostrom, who frequents the Extropians mailing list. (Usenet was still largely full of academics). In 1998, Nick Bostrom argues that a superintelligent AI might not necessarily be good or friendly, which along with other of Bostrom’s ideas will later become core to Yudkowsky.

In the year 2000, Yudkowsky founds the Singularity Institute for Artificial Intelligence, SIAI, later renamed to the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, MIRI. This appears to have started as a fake-it-til-you-make-it sort of thing, and it doesn’t pick up until he gets sponsored by Peter Thiel. Peter Thiel will be his largest sponsor until about 2015 or 2016. Now in 2026, Thiel has long since cut all ties, called this scene a “burning man camp” and “Luddite”, and called Yudkowsky the Antichrist.4

I forgot to mention this, and had to come back from later to add it: Jeffrey Epstein gave them fifty thousand dollars in 2009. One of the former presidents of MIRI is mentioned in Jeffrey Epstein’s emails5, which passes on effusive thanks for the visit to the island. (MIRI is documented as turning down his money in 2016 when he was much more notorious, if you want to figure out what to make of their statements about that.)

I considered putting all this in a footnote because of how unimportant Jeffrey Epstein’s appearance here is in the context of everything else. He is the Forrest Gump of evil shit. Of course he was here.

2009-2015: Writing, Community-Building

Eliezer Yudkowsky spends some time before 2009 blogging, and then contracts out setting up LessWrong as a customized version of Reddit’s code. In 2009, he bundles his last year or two of blog posts and puts them all on the newly-made LessWrong, where they come to be called The Sequences. Much later, in 2015, they are published as Rationality: From AI to Zombies. This is a series of essays about science and epistemology, most of them pretty closely related to books and ideas then in the zeitgeist but with both a very distinctly transhumanist (ie, “conquer death with technology”) and AI Doom thesis. It is written in such a way that it also works as, effectively, a self-help book about how to be better at thinking. This will later be something like the Rationalist Old Testament.

From 2010 to 2015, he writes HPMOR, and his audience becomes much larger, and this becomes a well-defined scene and people invested in the movement begin relocating to the Bay Area.

In 2010, Roko Mijic invents Roko’s Basilisk, which is most easily explained as the invention of Rationalist Pascal’s Wager, Rationalist Satan and Rationalist Hell, where those who fail to evangelize and help bring about the eschaton are sent. This will, over the years, drive those involved who are the most susceptible to religious mania and obsession insane. Yudkowsky disowns it immediately and tries to ban discussion of it from LessWrong, which makes it more popular.

At least as late as 2013, Yudkowsky is still advocating that we should make AI as long as we could do it safely.6 He is under the impression that his non-profit, MIRI, might be able to make “Friendly AI”, that is, one that does not kill everyone, ushers in the singularity and makes them immortal.

The Center for Applied Rationality, or CFAR, is founded in 2011 and offers classes. You essentially pay money for self-help, but it is primarily a recruiting front for MIRI, Yudkowsky’s actual operation. It also functions as a more-official avenue for community management, and seems to have managed peoples’ living situations and home lives much more than seems entirely normal, primarily via its alumni program.

They start a bunch of children’s camps, math camps, and study programs that are mostly still around. SPARC was the earliest, beginning in 2012, and takes high school students. All of its graduates from then will be adults now. Probably a bunch of them live in the Bay and work on AI safety.

Relocating to the Bay

Moving to the Bay Area worked for some people extremely well, and for others extremely badly. Much of this happened bottom-up, with members organizing things themselves, but in some specific cases you can tell who exactly is responsible for what.

I think of this as a flywheel, where the energy that keeps it moving is, fundamentally, their talent and their raw zeal for the cause. People show up, and they believe in what they’re doing, and they give what they can.

It is the best professional network on Earth. It is like being in the most elite fraternity, if it were gender-neutral and had many chapters in San Francisco specifically. If you have skills or can acquire them, you can have a fantastic job very quickly. There are a good number of coding bootcamps that will train you for and then place you at a job with no money up front. Since Peter Thiel is most of their funding, many of the connections are to companies he is invested in, but they have connections to essentially every company in the Valley.

Those people offer their work or their salaries to the cause.

Next tier down are people who can’t or don’t really use the opportunity that much, but who either end up doing something else or who end up doing work at the various rationalist non-profits. These people are fine, probably; CFAR probably takes some their money from them and they maybe could be doing better if they hadn’t spontaneously relocated to an extremely expensive city. Hopefully they really enjoy the scene.

Your bottom tier are people who are not particularly skilled, or who otherwise do not thrive in the Bay’s job and housing market. Many of them are runaways, even those that aren’t are often still teenagers, many of them have mental health problems. They are disproportionately trans, at least in part because trans teenagers are prone to getting thrown out of their houses.

Someone probably has to carry them, and they have nothing to offer but sex. Because this is a self-help, can-do ideology, often they spend all of their time trying to figure out what is wrong with them. They may be employed as some kind of household help for other people in the community, but this can actually be a transaction for sex. I have also heard of at least three people being effectively arranged-married within rationalism. I have no idea how that works.

All of this comes down to pulling more energy into the wheel, and you can trade each thing off against the other. Money can buy sex, sex can bring in money, both can be used for recruitment, influence and evangelism.

Any individual person or organization is really just bleeding energy off of the wheel. OpenAI, Anthropic, God knows how many smaller companies? They’re just pulling energy from this mass of eager, smart people that are already there. Successful ventures inject more funding and provide more connections to the movement, powering another turn of the wheel.

Recognizable cults, in contrast, are more like pure parasites.

2015-2018

This period sees Yudkowsky finish HPMOR and stop publishing, which leaves the community without a focus. As the most active and well-liked author still in the space, Scott Alexander becomes something like the Second Prophet of Rationalism. (People say these things as jokes sometimes, but this is pretty much accurate.) It seems to be much less focused leadership, though, and to some degree things start to drift.

Also in 2015, OpenAI is founded. This makes Google very sad because OpenAI exists to compete with Google on AI, and Yudkowsky knows and likes the Google guys, and he pronounces that the world is for sure going to end now, which he has continued doing for the last eleven years.

Oh, just one more thing. A former MIRI employee puts up a web site in late 2014 alleging that MIRI does no meaningful research and is primarily engaged in violations of statutory rape laws as well as legal damage control for those acts. MIRI will ultimately pay him something like $30,000 to go away and take down his site with those allegations.7

Rolling Stone, in 2025, pokes into this when writing a story about the Zizians.

The first set of allegations have been investigated and deemed baseless. They stem from a report filed by a onetime MIRI employee named Louie Helm who claimed a teenager was “being exploited” by a group of men, including Yudkowsky, who ran a local youth camp — referring to the Summer Program for Applied Rationality and Cognition, hosted by CFAR.

According to the sealed police report obtained by Rolling Stone, Helm accused Yudkowsky of having a sexual relationship with a then-18-year-old that began at least two and half years prior.

Officers were dispatched to Yudkowsky’s home, which, at the time, he shared with the 18-year-old in question. The “alleged victim,” officers wrote in the report, stressed that they “lived in a happy and safe environment.” That person later transitioned; today, he lives with his wife, whom he met in Berkeley’s Rationalist scene, and their two young children. When I spoke to him earlier this year, he told me he rejects the notion that he was exploited by anyone other than Helm, the disgruntled employee, whom he felt used him as ammunition against Yudkowsky and MIRI. “I was expedient,” he says.

What I find most interesting in this passage is that the alleged victim, speaking to Rolling Stone, denies “being exploited”. “Being exploited” sounds like, but is not, the same thing to deny as “statutory rape”. I am impressed that Yudkowsky is capable of living with an eighteen-year-old he is not related to as a thirty-five-year-old man, because that would annoy the shit out of me. I note that the question of whether the eighteen-year-old he lives with is, in fact, a person he met when they were fifteen, through a camp his organization runs, is neither asked nor answered in this passage.

Yudkowsky posted about 2000 words on twitter denying the allegation ahead of the Rolling Stone story coming out, and it seems to have blown over. Effective Altruists and Rationalists, like squid, spray ink when threatened.

Possibly because it needs someone more comfortable handling delicate and complex legal matters, in 2015 MIRI changes leadership. Nate Soares becomes President of MIRI, where he has been ever since as Yudkowsky’s right hand.

Brent Dill

I have no firsthand knowledge of this and know zero people involved so far as I am aware. I can only piece together what happened here from public records.8

Brent Dill was kicked out of the rationalist community for being very abusive to several girlfriends, and thereafter left San Francisco, apparently for lack of available housing.

There are several key details that made the allegations especially grim:

  1. He was significantly older.

  2. He exploited the victims’ financial and housing situations.

  3. He used BDSM concepts to justify doing things that are well over the line into abuse.

  4. Given the apparent pattern of escalation and lack of safe practices, it seems likely someone would have died eventually.

  5. Some of the accusations involve using MDMA to control his partners. MDMA is sometimes used for treating PTSD, and its use for this purpose was not unknown among the rationalists.

  6. He had access to children at a rationalist summer camp.

  7. Victims were pushed into mediation by CFAR, the rationalist self-help organization, which initially exonerated him. He was not punished until social media backlash led by two prominent people in the community who were, nevertheless, not official leadership.

What made this disturbing, also, is that this matched the pattern of abuse that was known to be common. Many people understood this coverup to be the sort of thing that could happen or would happen to them.

CFAR puts out this apology, which nobody seems to have found credible.

In general the community takes this pretty hard, and to their credit blames CFAR to a great degree. Between this and other scandals, demand for classes at CFAR seems to not be going well, and it stops offering classes in 2020. They started again November 2025, and you can currently sign up for a four-day applied rationality workshop if you can get past the waitlist.

Another interesting detail falls out of this, although it wouldn’t be public until much later. Brent has somewhat told his side of the story to a number of people, but most of it would be a tangent right now, and we will come back to it later. It is usually covered in redactions, funneled from unreliable sources or both. He would obviously have motive to lie. I am told, however, that these screenshots of his messages are legitimate. Really, the only important part here is “exposing how many ppl had sex with her as a minor”. He has been consistent about this detail over the years, to my understanding.

Brent Dill’s ouster also seems to have convinced a rationalist named Ziz Lasota, for whom the Zizians were named, that the earlier allegations from Louie Helm were true. She was already mostly an outcast from the rationalists, and had effectively thrown her career away to work for people who did not want her.
